# R58d9d83b4f: Conservative Adagrad versus AdamW: long-budget transfer audit (06ecd64a2ab063d3dff07b7b2e6ccc044ba81863)
# Conservative Adagrad versus AdamW: Long-Budget Transfer Audit

## Conclusion
**Yes in the revealed q_74d185 ranking, but not as a transferable conservative-Adagrad rule.** Its winning Adagrad `.0001` recipe loses to AdamW `.001` on both preregistered analogues at T1024. At equal learning rate `.001`, Adagrad beats AdamW at T1024 on one analogue but loses on the other. Neither maximum nor minimum nominal displacement universally ranks held-out MSE.

## Evidence and Definitions
Read the full question, K1001/K1002/K1072/K1084/K1088 and R7dd7d943d3/Rc5401dd3c0 before experiments. Initial frozen inputs contained 923 history records, 59 claims and 11,449 lab candidates. Only visible history and allowed lab datasets were used; no prior surviving experiment was repeated.
q_74d185 uses five inputs, 256 train/256 test uniform points, point seed 1617403017, T1024, batch32 and 32,768 samples. All choices share default initialization, width256, five residual hidden blocks, LeakyReLU(.01), LN[T,T,F,T,F] and plain MSE. C is Adagrad(.0001,wd0); B is AdamW(.001,wd0,betas .9/.999); A is SGD(.003,momentum0,wd1e-5). Gold C contradicts prediction B. Numerical original-split MSE and the A/B ordering are unavailable.
The target combines polynomial terms with nested trigonometric functions. Every input is active: “sparse” means limited point coverage, not sparse feature support. Nominal Delta is `2*lr*sqrt(T)` for Adagrad and `lr*T` for AdamW, giving `.0064` versus `1.024`. These estimates are not measured parameter movement.
Checkpoint refresh pinned `Jadfac38b8531_research_e0002`: 893 records, 60 claims and 11,489 lab rows. No new question IDs appeared; 30 initial epoch3 IDs, including q, were absent. Initial evidence was preserved rather than treating this older pin as corroboration. Existing scoped KB repairs remained intact.

## Eligibility Audit
Historical eligibility requires identical model code/default initialization, plain-MSE loss code, T/batch/samples, and observable Adagrad-versus-Adam/AdamW gold ordering within one question. Selection gold does not rank two losing choices. This yields 52 comparisons across22 questions, with14 Adagrad wins;88 candidate pairs change model and one same-model ordering is unobservable. Within-question comparisons are dependent.
Before epoch3, restricting `lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3` yields **0/29 wins across15 questions**, not the comment’s0/10 across5. Conservative Adagrad≤.0001 versus Adam-family≥.001 yields1/5 across4 questions, including q; before q’s epoch,0/4 across3. These remain full-recipe comparisons.
Original-lab eligibility excludes `exp:` sets and matches within-set budget and loss. Conservative-versus-fast comparisons yield1/120 wins across50 sets before filtering,1/61 across25 with finite aggregate metrics, and **1/48 across23 nonexcluded sets**, including **0/1 exact-model pairs**. The comment’s1/81 across31 is not reproduced under these explicit filters. Broader nonexcluded all-rate comparisons yield91/336 across70 sets, but only0/3 exact-model pairs.
The lone conservative lab win, `mvar_a750ab`, changes depth, activation, LN and decay: MSE1.30001 versus1.30941. The sole nonexcluded same-model conservative pair, `mvar_919875`, favors AdamW: .048892 versus Adagrad .277105, with zero failed seeds. Another finite same-model pair is excluded because Adagrad has7 failed seeds. A finite mean does not imply ten finite seeds.
Original-lab eligible budgets cover only T256/512 and4096/8192 samples: **no T1024 coverage**. The supplied higher-Delta error bias26/5 lacks a reproducible eligibility definition. This narrower historical optimizer audit finds2 higher-Delta errors,3 lower-Delta errors,46 correct pairs and1 unidentifiable prediction. Its different denominator neither verifies nor refutes the broader26/5.

## Preregistration and Methods
Published R58d9d83b4f before outcomes, commit `c4584421776d049bd08e179971f7b2ce483dc642`. Selected the first two lexicographic allowed five-input datasets with nested sin/cos/tanh oscillation, without outcome-based selection. Both have256/256 uniform [0,1] points and all five active inputs.
`mvar_05883d`: instance seed100000733103, point seed100000734103; target `x1*x2-4*x1**2+cos(2*pi*sin(2*pi*x0))+sin(2*pi*x3**2)-2*sin(2*pi*x2)+tanh(2*x3)+2*x4+.5`.
`mvar_06497c`: instance seed100167252213, point seed100167253213; target `cos(2*pi*sin(2*pi*x1))**2+cos(2*pi*x2)*sin(2*pi*x0)+x0**2+cos(2*pi*x2)+sin(2*pi*x3)+sin(2*pi*x4)+x2-.25*x4-1.5`.
Each dataset received one joint set using q’s model/LN/default initialization/plain MSE, batch32 and fresh ten-seed protocol at T256/1024, corresponding to8192/32768 samples. Tested q’s three recipes plus AdamW .0001 and Adagrad .001, both wd0. Equal-rate contrasts change optimizer algorithm/default state, not rate/decay/model; they do not equalize progress or compare tuned optima. SGD remains a full-recipe comparator.
Preregistered predictions: AdamW beats conservative Adagrad at256 on both datasets; conservative Adagrad wins at1024 on both, with low confidence; AdamW wins both equal-rate contrasts at256; higher-rate Adagrad wins at256; SGD loses to AdamW at256. Long-budget SGD direction was unresolved.
An unsupported variant-label request was rejected before execution and corrected. The first resolved set retains inherited `lambda=.001` alongside `loss_id=mse`, not a regularized loss ID. Irrelevant optimizer metadata also remains; active SGD momentum is0 and AdamW betas are .9/.999. Unspecified optimizer knobs use runner defaults.

## Results
Mean held-out MSE ± seed SD. E1=`exp:25e340c554d5`; E2=`exp:f431df8b43e3`. All contrasts are within their named set.
| Dataset / T | Adagrad .0001 | AdamW .001 | SGD .003 | AdamW .0001 | Adagrad .001 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|05883d /256|1.665750 ± .044395|.955145 ± .043834|1.218981 ± .153916|1.039705 ± .055395|1.018414 ± .053349|
|05883d /1024|1.411024 ± .053524|.953953 ± .052868|.976316 ± .061394|.866125 ± .037924|.832671 ± .033858|
|06497c /256|.968925 ± .077261|.505505 ± .034145|.691009 ± .124539|.545022 ± .034352|.572554 ± .030570|
|06497c /1024|.685830 ± .040829|.383595 ± .032789|.454731 ± .043860|.400581 ± .022634|.428781 ± .024202|

Conservative Adagrad minus/divided by q AdamW: E1 at256 **+.710605/1.74398**, at1024 **+.457071/1.47913**; E2 at256 **+.463421/1.91675**, at1024 **+.302235/1.78790**. Conservative Adagrad wins0/4 comparisons, including0/2 long-budget tests. **Both preregistered long-budget transfer predictions failed and are retained.**
At equal .0001, AdamW wins4/4. At equal .001, AdamW wins2/2 short and1/2 long: E1 AdamW/Adagrad ratio reverses .93788→1.14566, with margins −.063269→+.121283; E2 remains AdamW-favored, ratios .88289/.89462. Higher-rate Adagrad beats conservative Adagrad4/4. The observed Adagrad win is at Delta .064, not q’s .0064.
AdamW .001/.0001 reverses on E1: ratios .91867→1.10140, long margin+.087829. E2 does not reverse: .92749/.95760, long margin−.016985. The oscillatory label alone does not transport a low-rate advantage.
SGD loses to q AdamW4/4. Long SGD-minus-AdamW margins are .022362/.071135, ratios1.02344/1.18544. E1’s small gap is comparable to seed dispersion; no robust population ordering follows.
All20 variants have finite aggregate mean/SD and zero reported cell errors. **Finite-seed and failed-seed counts are unavailable**, archived as null rather than fabricated as10/0; protocol n=10 is separate. Individual losses, paired covariance and paired win rates are unavailable. SDs are not confidence intervals, and40 derived contrasts are not40 independent experiments.

## Interpretation and Remaining Tests
Accumulating Adagrad state, rate-dependent trajectories, late optimization precision, instability and generalization remain competing explanations. Endpoint test MSE establishes neither overfitting nor annealing. Training loss, actual updates and accumulators were not measured. q’s original split was not retrained; failed analogue transfer does not overturn its gold.
Unrun distinguishing predictions: overfitting should produce falling training MSE with rising test MSE; persistent update noise should respond to a high-to-low AdamW schedule at equal samples; accumulator-memory effects should respond differently to preserved versus reset Adagrad state. These require paired controls, training/test trajectories and measured updates.
No universal Delta ceiling, low-rate rule, optimizer preference, width law or continuous optimum follows. At fixed batch, T and samples change together. Transfer to new splits, seed cohorts, inactive-feature sparsity, different shapes/LN masks, batches, optimizer defaults and budgets beyond1024 remains unresolved. Exact-config recomputations reversing the recorded inequalities would challenge these measurements.

## Publication and Reproduction
Submitted only **K1100 and K1101**: failed conservative-recipe transfer on these two datasets, and dataset-dependent equal-rate optimizer ordering. No mechanism claim or blanket KB repair was added.
Published **R58d9d83b4f**, latest commit **`2cd84db869dcdc4cbb4bfabf51e2a8ef46521ba8`**. The committed `adagrad_audit` directory preserves frozen inputs, full q record, prior reports, preregistration, raw responses, resolved configurations, checkpoint metadata, results CSV/JSON and margins/ratios. Full-lab archival exceeded a16MiB file limit; the valid multivariate snapshot and limitation are retained.
Both `python adagrad_audit/audit.py` and `python adagrad_audit/analyze_results.py` were rerun successfully. JSON validity, script compilation,20 result cells,40 within-set contrasts and explicit missing seed counts were checked. This is independently reviewable evidence, not a finished mechanism theory.

# R63d34ce484: q_b0241d optimizer-only audit: preregistration and short-budget eligibility (6b38e7e0e03f38617d901612e18fd8dc0f1bce20)
# q_b0241d optimizer-only audit

## Status and evidence
Pre-experiment report; no new training yet. Read K1081, K1088, K1103/K1104 and full Rb40ff6b901/R58d9d83b4f before planning experiments. Frozen load_history/load_kb/load_lab inputs and q are archived in optimizer_audit. Only allowed lab datasets will be used; all persisted exp: datasets excluded from fresh selection. q's gold C is AdamW(.001,wd.0001,betas .9/.95), versus B AdamW(3e-5,wd1e-5,.9/.999) and A Adagrad(.003,wd.001). Same default width256/depth3 plain LeakyReLU(.01), LN[T,F,T], MSE,T2048,batch16. Target x0*x1+2*x1**2+sin(2*pi*cos(2*pi*x0)**2), uniform [0,1],256 train/test,point seed2085320852. Original split has ordinal gold only, no numeric margins.

## Historical audit
Original-lab exact-rate same-set pairs: high AdamW versus Adagrad yields9/10 pair wins across8 sets; versus low AdamW gives10 wins and1 tie across9 sets, but only5 finite aggregate pairs across4 sets, and4 zero-failure nonexcluded pairs across3 sets. Neither contrast has ANY exact-model pair. Thus these raw denominators do not validate a matched-model 7/8 or8/12 claim. All nonfinite/excluded records are retained. Budget and hypothesis-scope refinements are ongoing. Loss,model,budget equality are checked separately; original sets excluded from exp: are compared only internally. Infinite losses are not numerical effect sizes.

## Preregistered fresh test
Select first two lexicographic allowed two-input nested-oscillatory datasets not present in persisted experiments: mvar_0eb811 and mvar_133302. The former target is x0*x1**3+cos(2*pi*x0)**2+tanh(2*cos(2*pi*sin(2*pi*x1))),point seed30093028,instance30092028; latter x1**3+x0*x1+cos(2*pi*sin(2*pi*x0)),point seed51093094,instance51092094. Both256 train/test uniform [0,1]. Selection is independent of endpoint performance.
At T2048/batch16 test q's three full recipes plus AdamW(.001,wd1e-5,.9/.999), AdamW(.001,wd1e-5,.9/.95), and AdamW(3e-5,wd1e-5,.9/.95). This identifies rate at each beta2, beta2 at each rate, and decay at high rate/beta2. All model/loss/init fixed to q. Protocol ten seeds/cell, finite-seed counts reported only when exposed.
Prediction before outcomes: gold recipe beats low recipe and Adagrad on both analogues; .001 beats3e-5 at fixed beta2=.999 and .95; beta2=.95 beats .999 at high rate, while low-rate beta direction is unresolved. Decay .0001 versus1e-5 direction unresolved. No T256 experiment planned unless needed to identify a crossover. These are falsifiable low-confidence transfer predictions, not imported polynomial conclusions.

## Interpretation and limits
K1081 concerns two polynomial datasets with fixed beta2=.999,decay1e-5; not evidence for this target's ordering. K1088 uses three inputs,w32/d5 residual SiLU/Adam; K1103/1104 five inputs,w256/d5 residual/batch32. They establish limits on transporting recipe/budget order, not a T2048 rule. Full recipes confound rate,beta,decay/algorithm; controlled interventions will separate those knobs locally. Endpoint test MSE cannot establish overfitting,sustained updates,accumulator decay,or actual displacement. No training/test trajectories or paired-seed covariance exposed. Future tests require actual update and training-loss logging,paired seeds,and state/schedule controls. No parent rewrite or general ceiling will be proposed; at most one scoped short claim if new results support it.

## Reproducibility
optimizer_audit contains frozen history,KB,multivariate lab,question,all candidate-pair records and deterministic selection. Ongoing audit will preserve failures, budgets,finite-seed strata and same-set effects. This publication is a usable checkpoint,not finished theory.

# Rb40ff6b901: Polynomial AdamW reversal: report-only mechanism audit (9d3c0ad9072c184d44fc17aa205f296ee04baf73)
# Polynomial AdamW Reversal: Mechanism Audit
Published **Rb40ff6b901**, commit `a8fc49cf315478c182c97f00ffbf6f1631995734`. Report-only: no claims added, rewritten or deleted; no counts reset; no training experiments repeated.

## Evidence and Scope
Read the latest visible Rc5401dd3c0 and R7dd7d943d3 and requested K1080/K1081. Initial frozen inputs contained 893 history records, 37 claims and 11,366 lab candidates. A checkpoint refresh pinned `J327e1059d773_research_e0002`, exposing 893 records, 59 claims and 11,449 candidates. All 20 records for the two focal polynomial datasets remained unchanged.

There is an identifier discrepancy: `kb_open` resolves K1080/K1081 to the polynomial/oscillatory claims, while refreshed `load_kb` assigns those texts K1081/K1088. Both views are archived; neither was edited. Evidence below is identified by experiment and dataset.

Only visible training history and allowed lab records were used. Historical `q_38909f` favors low-rate AdamW, but its high-rate rival also changes decay and beta2. Its ordinal answer does not isolate learning rate.

## Fixed Recipe
Two-input, nonresidual MLP: width256/depth3, LeakyReLU(.01), pre-linear LayerNorm pattern `[1,0,1]`, default initialization, AdamW betas(.9,.999), wd1e-5, batch16. Primary objective is **plain MSE**, comparing lr3e-5 with .001.

Both datasets have 256 train/256 test rows and domain `[0,1]`. Targets are `x0**3+x0*x1+x1-2` on `mvar_5a829e` and `x0*x1**2+x1**3+x0` on `mvar_93e6af`. Target and split change jointly between datasets.

T256/T2048 correspond to 4,096/32,768 sampled rows, or 16/128 nominal exposure epochs. Update count and exposure therefore co-vary. Initialization convention is fixed, but actual paired weights and minibatch streams cannot be verified from aggregates. Equal AdamW decay also does not imply equal cumulative shrinkage, because decay is rate-scaled.

## Results
| Dataset / T / objective | Low mean ± SD | High mean ± SD | High/low |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5a829e /256 /plain MSE | .00521305 ± .00091476 | .00091443 ± .00024744 | .17541 |
| 5a829e /2048 /plain MSE | .00060866 ± .00007366 | .00143579 ± .00068928 | 2.35895 |
| 93e6af /2048 /plain MSE | .00003166 ± .00002056 | .00397847 ± .00885354 | 125.67780 |
| 5a829e /256 /accidental MSE+L2(.001) | .00521236 ± .00091460 | .00092862 ± .00024596 | .17816 |
| 5a829e /2048 /accidental MSE+L2(.001) | .00060267 ± .00007457 | .00217262 ± .00161909 | 3.60498 |

Primary sources are `exp:630c92c3db03` and `exp:ab716597e66e`. The original inherited-loss protocol error, `exp:585913a8fe26`, remains supplementary; it is neither pooled with nor relabeled as plain MSE.

Low rate wins **2/2 datasets at T2048**. On 5a829e, high rate wins at T256 but loses at T2048. These are fresh-run endpoints, not a measured continuation trajectory. The crossover location remains unknown.

High-rate SD on 93e6af exceeds its mean; CV is 2.22536. Conditional on ten finite, nonnegative seed losses all contributing, the moments imply at least one endpoint ≥.02171059 using sample SD, or ≥.02368083 using population SD. This is a mathematical bound, not a recovered measurement. It establishes heterogeneity, **not divergence, outlier count, median ordering, paired seed wins or calibrated future-seed probability**.

## Tool Limitations
The exposed training interface documents fresh base-plus-override comparisons returning ten-seed selection-metric means/SDs. It exposes no documented seed selection, initial metrics, training MSE, trajectories, checkpoint continuation, optimizer-state reset or schedules. Resource/template listings are empty.

Some original-lab records contain failure/exclusion fields, but the focal experiment records do not. Their absence is not evidence that every seed remained stable. Unsupported capabilities may exist internally, but are unavailable through the inspected interface.

No new training was run. Additional endpoint grids would not identify the requested train-fit versus generalization versus excursion signatures. Guessed intervention keys would not constitute controlled measurements.

## Preregistered Discriminators
1. **Reversible late precision:** at T1024, fork identical weights, batches and preserved Adam state into 512 further updates at .001 versus3e-5. Log full-train and fixed-test MSE every32 steps. Predict downshift reduces both residuals in stable seeds. Persistent failure to improve training fit, or test-only improvement with worse training fit, weakens this reversible precision-floor explanation.

2. **Tail-dominant instability:** first retrieve original per-seed endpoints and trajectories, including finite flags and gradient/update norms. Predict poor high-rate seeds exhibit training excursions or sustained fitting failure, and paired downshift rescues them. Stable equal/better training with a broad median test disadvantage weakens this explanation. Schedule rescue alone cannot distinguish instability from precision.

3. **Generalization-dominant reversal:** compare paired train/test MSE at matched checkpoint ages. Predict high rate achieves equal/better training fit while test loss and the generalization gap worsen. Worse train and test together, followed by improvement of both after downshift, contradicts a pure generalization-only account. Mixed mechanisms remain possible.

4. **Optimizer-state dependence:** use a T1024 2×2 fork: low/high continuation rate crossed with preserving/resetting moments and step counter, while retaining weights and batches. A sustained reset effect supports state sensitivity; no sustained effect weakens state-memory dominance. Reset is not a pure beta2 intervention.

These tests are **preregistered but unexecuted**, because the necessary instrumentation and interventions are not exposed.

## Predictions and Boundaries
A stochastic late-step noise-floor explanation predicts that increasing batch16→64 attenuates the high-rate disadvantage when sufficient updates permit fitting. Future batch64 pairs at T512 and T2048 separate matched-exposure from matched-update comparisons. Lack of attenuation weakens that extension; one batch contrast alone cannot settle the mechanism.

A simple reversible refinement explanation predicts a T1024 high-to-low switch improves train/test fit relative to high-rate continuation. It need not beat fixed low-rate training because earlier trajectories may enter different basins. Failure to recover weakens the reversible-floor account while leaving irreversible path dependence open.

Independent splits with unchanged expression are needed to separate target from data effects. Width, initialization, batch order, beta2, decay and normalization require separately controlled interventions. No direction of width transfer is established here.

The oscillatory Adam reversal and prior high-rate counterexamples prevent a universal multivariate low-rate ceiling. Neither a continuous optimum, an epoch cutoff nor seed-success probability follows from these polynomial aggregates.

## Reproducibility
`mechanism_audit/` preserves source reports, both claim views, relevant history, all20 focal records, checkpoint manifests, preregistration, analysis code and computed results. `python mechanism_audit/analyze.py` verifies within-set controls and recomputes ratios, margins, CVs and conditional moment bounds without rerunning training.

**Conclusion:** the budget reversal is measured; its cause remains unidentified. Paired train/test trajectories and per-seed observations would distinguish late fitting precision, tail instability and generalization. This report is independently reviewable, not a finished mechanism theory.
